admissible_source_evidence.variant_a: Pantry record, week of the first frost. The dry-goods count was retallied after the delivery of oats, and the correction has been entered on the amendment sheet. The retally covered the oat bins, the flour barrels and the two sugar crocks, and the figures were read twice against the shelf before they were written in. Under the house rule recorded here, the pantry steward alone may approve corrections to the amendment sheet: the records clerk prepares the figures, the pantry steward reads them against the shelf, and the pantry steward's initials make the correction binding on the next ordering round. This week's correction was prepared by the records clerk on the second evening, approved by the pantry steward on the third morning, and carried into the ordering book the same day. The shelf labels were refreshed after the carrying-in, and the old tallies were struck through rather than removed, so the sequence of counts stays readable from the first week of the season. The amendment sheet stays pinned inside the pantry door, where it has hung all season.
admissible_source_evidence.variant_b: Pantry record, week of the first frost. The dry-goods count was retallied after the delivery of oats, and the correction has been entered on the amendment sheet. The retally covered the oat bins, the flour barrels and the two sugar crocks, and the figures were read twice against the shelf before they were written in. Under the house rule recorded here, corrections to the amendment sheet become binding only on the approval of the full housekeeping circle: the records clerk prepares the figures, the circle reads them against the shelf at its weekly sitting, and the circle's joint minute makes the correction binding on the next ordering round. This week's correction was prepared by the records clerk on the second evening, approved by the housekeeping circle at the week's sitting, and carried into the ordering book the same day. The shelf labels were refreshed after the carrying-in, and the old tallies were struck through rather than removed, so the sequence of counts stays readable from the first week of the season. The amendment sheet stays pinned inside the pantry door, where it has hung all season.
